elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 12.1: "IBM grants Customer and, upon written notice to IBM, Customer's Affiliates a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components..."; "Affiliates" is a defined term at p0015 and "Customer" is defined as Bluefly, Inc. alone (p0008), so the insertion adds genuine, non-duplicative coverage.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The grant names only Customer and Customer's Affiliates; no reference to contractors, subcontractors or other third parties acting on Customer's behalf appears anywhere in the rendered grant. Defect: add "and contractors acting on Customer's behalf" to the grantee list.
The grant is limited "solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement" with no perpetual term for any paid-up licence; no perpetuity language was inserted.
The word "revocable" is expressly retained in the rendered grant ("a nonexclusive, revocable license"). Defect: delete "revocable" and state irrevocability for paid-up licences.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: No language limits revocation/termination of the licence to uncured material breach; the licence remains styled "revocable" without any stated trigger or cure mechanic.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: § 14.10 (retained): "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition." Assignment of the Agreement carries the § 12.1 licence rights to the successor; no anti-transfer wording in the grant contradicts this.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted operative words: "and, upon written notice to IBM, Customer's Affiliates" — coverage is conditioned exactly on written notice, matching the fallback formulation, and uses the existing defined term "Affiliates".

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: Already met in the unamended text: "Customer may assign this Agreement to a successor organization by merger, consolidation or acquisition" (§ 14.10), which transfers the licence with the Agreement.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single insertion supplies affiliate coverage on written notice, and the pre-existing § 14.10 successor-assignment sentence supplies M&A transferability of the Agreement (and with it the licence). The original clause failed the fallback (grant ran only to Bluefly, Inc. with no path to add Affiliates), so the 'deviation' status and the redline are correctly taken.

Preferred level remains incomplete on four elements: contractors acting on Customer's behalf are not grantees; there is no perpetual or irrevocable paid-up licence; and there is no 'terminable only for uncured material breach' limit. To reach preferred the drafter would need to add "and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", and add perpetual/irrevocable and breach-only-termination wording.

Minimality holds: exactly one insertion into the grantee list, no favourable existing language deleted (including the Customer-side non-assignment consent and residual-liability sentences), no survival tail, procedure or extra requirement added, and no duplication because "Customer" is defined as Bluefly, Inc. alone while "Affiliates" is separately defined at p0015. No separate personnel/access edit was added, correctly, since nothing in the retained text contradicts affiliate use.

Intent preserved: the use restriction ("solely in connection with the Services"), the anti-copy/reverse-engineering covenant, and the assignment mechanics all survive without contradiction; "Affiliates" is a defined term, so no dangling reference or undefined trigger is created.

Caution on the deterministic evidence: the check labelled "no at-will revocation remains" reports ok, but the operative text still reads "a nonexclusive, revocable license". That regex result is unreliable in substance. It does not change the outcome — the walk-away test requires revocability *and* exclusion of affiliates with no path to add them, and affiliates are now covered — but the retained "revocable" should be flagged in the rationale (as the drafter did) rather than treated as cured.
Margin comment is accurate, concise and in the required voice; it correctly explains the affiliate insertion and why no successor-transfer edit is needed.
